title: Influence of electronic correlations on disorder-induced loop currents in high-Tc superconductors
abstract: Time-reversal symmetry breaking in superconducting systems can manifest itself in the form of currents which are induced by inhomogeneities in the charge and order parameter distribution. With regard to cuprates such states have been theoretically studied in the overdoped region of the phase diagram where the inhomogeneities are related to out-of plane dopants. In this paper we will extend previous work by including local correlations within the unrestricted Gutzwiller approximation in order to study its impact on the induced loop currents. In addition, we investigate the effect of next-nearest neighbor hopping which extends the TRSB phase towards half-filling. We find that in general correlations lead to a suppression of loop currents, however, the Gutzwiller approach can sustain such states to larger values of the local on-site repulsion as compared to the Hartree-Fock approximation. Our investigations allow for an estimation of the local magnetic moment emerging from impurity-induced loop currents for cuprate superconductors.
summary: This theoretical work examines disorder-induced loop currents in high-Tc superconductors by incorporating strong electronic correlations using the Gutzwiller Approximation. The research compares these results against simpler Hartree-Fock treatments, finding that while correlations generally suppress currents, GA allows for stable superconducting states under stronger repulsive interactions than HF. This provides insights into local magnetism arising from impurities in cuprates.
main_problem: The study investigates how electronic correlations affect loop currents induced by disorder within high-Tc superconductors.
main_result: While general correlations suppress loop currents compared to Hartree-Fock, the Gutzwiller Approximation (GA) can sustain superconducting states up to higher on-site repulsion ($U$) than HF predicts.
method: The authors use theoretical modeling involving the unrestricted Gutzwiller Approximation and solving the Bogoliubov-de Gennes equations iteratively.
model_or_system: The system is based on an extended single-band Hubbard Hamiltonian applied to cuprate superconductors, incorporating local disorder and inter-site interactions.
key_observables: Induced loop currents ($\langle j_{ij} angle$), local magnetic moments, and the superconducting order parameter structure (characterized by $\alpha = \arctan(\Delta_d/\Delta_s)$).
important_parameters: Local repulsion ($U/t$), doping concentration ($\langle n angle$), and hopping ratios ($t'/t$).
main_assumptions: The primary approximations used are the Unrestricted Gutzwiller Approximation (GA) and comparison against the Hartree-Fock (HF) decoupling.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate phase diagrams showing superconducting state stability ($\alpha$ vs $t'/t$) for both HF and GA, alongside visualizations of current patterns around impurities and average current strength dependence on doping.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the theoretical framework (Hamiltonian, methods), then analyzing how correlations affect the superconducting phase diagram ($s+id$ stability), and finally quantifying the resulting disorder-induced loop currents in both single and multiple impurity scenarios.
why_interesting: Although focused on cuprates, the use of advanced many-body approximations like GA to study correlated ground states under external perturbations (disorder) is relevant for understanding complex quantum phases in strongly interacting systems.
